tldr: This is a loose research cluster, not one event: early November papers covered RL theory, orchestration benchmarks, and KV-cache memory for co-resident agents. From Nov 4 the work tilted toward securing multi-agent systems and attributing their failures, from NIST identity tenets to CoLFA and AgentLeak.
whats_new: Two new papers push from diagnosis to repair: TRACE-MAS (Nov 17) diagnoses and repairs collaboration failures between agents, and Kaer (Nov 18) adds security-aware replanning to orchestrators that revise plans mid-run.
why_it_matters: The open problems in multi-agent stacks are now securing, debugging, and paying for them: agent identity, data leakage, which agent caused a failure, how to repair it, and KV-cache memory per resident agent.

beats.headline: RL theory for open systems and WorkflowArena, a benchmark for worker-spawning workflows
beats.summary: One theory paper on partially controllable agents and one executable orchestration benchmark anchor the coordination side of the thread.

beats.headline: Security and privacy become the dominant thread, from NIST guidance to an open-source leak tester
beats.summary: NIST identity tenets, private retrieval, secure aggregation against malicious agents, and AgentLeak all target what one agent can see, claim, or leak.

beats.headline: Memory and serving cost: coordinated KV-cache quantization, agent-designed serving, LinkedIn's distillation
beats.summary: Only the KV-cache paper is multi-agent-specific; ServerBench and the LinkedIn talk are adjacent serving work the clustering pulled in.

beats.headline: From attributing failures to repairing them: CoLFA, TRACE-MAS, and Kaer
beats.summary: CoLFA names the faulty step and agent; TRACE-MAS repairs collaboration failures; Kaer replans with security constraints when tasks fail.

open_questions: Does any open-source agent framework adopt per-agent identity along the lines of NIST's design tenets?
Does AgentLeak gain users or published results against real frameworks beyond its Show HN launch?
Does WorkflowArena get adopted as a shared orchestration benchmark by other papers?
Does coordinated KV-cache quantization ship in a serving engine that hosts several agents per GPU?
Do TRACE-MAS or Kaer release code that works with an existing orchestration framework?
take_for_builders: Log which agent produced each message and plan revision, and scope each agent's credentials, so you can attribute failures and leaks; treat the repair and replanning papers as research until code is released and replicated.
